scenarios.title: {DAD} Wants to Be Your Agent
scenarios.text: {DAD} has printed business cards. They say '{DAD}: Football Management'. He wants to handle {J}'s next contract himself. 'Who better than family?' he says.
scenarios.prompt: Let your father manage your career?

choices.label: Gently say no
choices.text: {DAD} goes quiet for a week. Then he puts the business cards in a drawer and asks to come to every match instead.

choices.label: Give him an advisory role
choices.desc: He sits in on meetings. The agent negotiates.
choices.text: {DAD} sits in every meeting in his best shirt, asks one question each time, and is very proud. The agent tolerates it.

choices.label: Let him do it
choices.hint: He means well. He doesn't know the business.
choices.text: {DAD} negotiates the next deal himself. He's tough, funny and hopelessly out of his depth. The club gets a bargain.

scenarios.title: {MUM} and {DAD}
scenarios.text: {MUM} calls him late at night. She's been crying. She and {DAD} have been sleeping in separate rooms for months, and now she's talking about leaving.
scenarios.prompt: Your parents' marriage is falling apart.

choices.label: Go home and talk to both of them
choices.hint: You can't fix it. You can be present.

out.text: He sits them both down. It's the first honest conversation they've had in years. They agree to see a counsellor. It might work.
He listens to both sides until 3am. They separate anyway. He tells {SIB} the news himself.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.text: He tells {MUM} he loves her and that it's their decision. She says she understands. She also says she wishes he'd come home.

scenarios.title: A Cousin Calls
text: A cousin he last saw at a wedding when he was nine calls with a business idea and a request for {ask}.
An uncle needs {ask} for a motorbike, his daughter's wedding and 'a small debt'. He says it's a loan. Everybody knows it isn't.
An aunt he barely knows messages him: her son needs {ask} for university. She attaches a photo of herself holding {J} as a baby.
scenarios.prompt: A relative wants {ask}.

choices.label: Give it
choices.text: He sends it. The relative is grateful. Within a month, three more relatives have called.

choices.label: Give half, with honesty
choices.text: He sends half and explains, kindly, that he can't fund everyone. The relative sulks, then thanks him.

choices.label: Let {MUM} decide who gets help
choices.text: {MUM} becomes the family's minister of finance. She is ruthless and fair. Requests drop by half.

choices.label: Say no
choices.text: He says no. By the weekend, half the family has heard that he's 'changed'.

scenarios.title: The Family Bank
scenarios.text: Since he started helping relatives, a spreadsheet would be useful. He doesn't have one. {MUM} does: it's long, and it's mostly people who 'will pay back next month'.
scenarios.prompt: The family sees you as a bank.

choices.label: Set up a family fund with rules
choices.text: A family fund: school fees, medical bills, emergencies. Nothing else. Some relatives grumble; the important things get paid.

choices.label: Keep saying yes
choices.text: He keeps saying yes. The requests keep coming. His accountant sends a worried email.

choices.label: Close the bank
choices.hint: Peace for your wallet. War at family gatherings.
choices.text: He closes the bank. The next family wedding is very frosty.

scenarios.title: {SIB}'s Secret
scenarios.text: {SIB} calls in a panic: online loans, one to pay another, then another. {SIBhe} owes {debt} and the lenders have started calling {MUM}.
scenarios.prompt: Your {SIBr} is in debt.

choices.label: Pay it off, with a serious talk
choices.text: He pays every lender and sits {SIB} down for a long, uncomfortable talk about money. {SIBhe} cries. {SIBhe} also listens.

choices.label: Pay it off quietly, no questions
choices.text: He pays it off without a word. {SIB} is grateful. Six months later the lenders call again.

choices.label: Make {SIBhim} sort it out
choices.text: He refuses to pay but helps {SIB} make a repayment plan. It takes {SIBhim} two years. {SIBhe} never borrows again.

scenarios.title: {SIB} Wants to Play
scenarios.text: {SIB} has been playing football at {SIBplace} and is actually good. A local academy wants {SIBhim} on trial. Everyone at home keeps saying, 'just like {SIBhis} big brother.'
scenarios.prompt: Your {SIBr} wants to be a footballer too.

choices.label: Train with {SIBhim} and help
choices.text: Every off-day, he trains {SIB} in the park. {SIBhe} gets into the academy. The comparisons never stop, but {SIBhe} doesn't seem to mind.

choices.label: Warn {SIBhim} how hard it is
choices.text: He tells {SIB} about the injuries, the loneliness, the rejection. {SIBhe} listens, then says, 'I still want to.' Respect.

choices.label: Pay for the best academy
choices.text: He pays for a private academy. {SIB} thrives, and is also the only kid there whose brother is on TV.

scenarios.title: {SIB}'s Debut
scenarios.text: {SIB} is making {SIBhis} professional debut this weekend for a club in the lower leagues. The whole family is going. {J} has a match the same day.
scenarios.prompt: Your {SIBr}'s debut is on the same day as your match.

choices.label: Watch on your phone in the dressing room
choices.text: He watches the stream on his phone until the last minute before his own warm-up. {SIB} plays forty minutes. {J} cries in the toilets.

choices.label: Ask the manager to let you miss your match

out.text: Amazingly, {Mf} says yes. He's in the stands when {SIB} comes on. {SIB} sees him and almost forgets to run.
{Mf} says no, firmly. He watches the highlights on the bus.

scenarios.title: Grandmother
text: His grandmother, the one who used to feed him after every school match, is in hospital. The doctors are using careful words. {MUM} says she keeps asking for him.
His grandmother is very ill. She has watched every one of his matches on a tiny TV, even the ones at three in the morning.
scenarios.prompt: Your grandmother is very ill.

choices.label: Go to her now
choices.text: He sits by her bed for two days. She holds his hand and tells him stories about his father as a boy. She dies peacefully a week later. He was there.

choices.label: Video call every day
choices.desc: Be there the only way you can.
choices.text: Every day, a video call. She can barely speak, but she smiles every time. She dies on a Tuesday. He finds out during training.

scenarios.title: {MUM}'s Dream
scenarios.text: {MUM} has dreamed of making the pilgrimage to Mecca her whole life. She has been saving for twenty years and has a third of what she needs. She would never ask.
scenarios.prompt: Pay for your parents' pilgrimage ({cost})?

choices.label: Pay for both of them
choices.text: When he tells her, {MUM} can't speak. {DAD} has to sit down. They leave in the spring and call him from Mecca in tears.

choices.label: Pay for {MUM}, add to the savings
choices.text: With his help, {MUM}'s twenty years of saving are finally enough. She goes. She brings him back a prayer mat.

scenarios.title: {MUM} Has Opinions
text: {MUM} has decided {Pf} doesn't dress appropriately, doesn't cook properly and doesn't call often enough. She says all of this to {J}. Some of it to {Pf}.
{DAD} thinks {Pf} is 'after the money'. He hasn't said it to her. He's said it to everyone else.
scenarios.prompt: Your parents and your partner don't get on.

choices.label: Defend {Pf} to your parents
choices.hint: Your partner will remember. So will your parents.
choices.text: He tells {MUM} and {DAD} that {Pf} is family now, and that's the end of it. It isn't the end of it, but things improve.

choices.label: Get them all around one table

out.text: Somewhere between the main course and dessert, {MUM} and {Pf} discover a shared hatred of a TV presenter. Peace.
Dinner ends with {Pf} in the car and {MUM} in tears. He sits between two silences.

choices.label: Avoid the subject
choices.text: He keeps them apart. Christmas is two dinners now.

scenarios.title: {DAD}'s Shop
scenarios.text: {DAD}'s little shop has been struggling for years. A supermarket opened down the road. He wants {cost} to renovate and fight back. He doesn't want charity: he wants an investor.
scenarios.prompt: Invest in your father's shop?

choices.label: Invest as a real partner
choices.hint: Could revive it. Could sink money.

out.text: The renovated shop, with a signed shirt in the window, becomes a local landmark. Queues on matchdays.
The supermarket wins. The shop closes a year later. {DAD} is heartbroken, but grateful he tried.

choices.label: Suggest he retire instead
choices.text: {DAD} takes it as an insult, then as a relief. He closes the shop and spends his days at the mosque and the market, talking about his son.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Welcome
scenarios.text: His hometown wants to hold a parade for him: a convertible, a marching band, a mural on the side of his old school. {MUM} has already bought a new outfit.
scenarios.prompt: Accept the hometown parade?

choices.label: Accept, and bring the whole family
choices.desc: Their day as much as yours.
choices.text: Thousands line the streets. His old PE teacher cries. {DAD} waves from the car like a president. The mural is beautiful and slightly wrong.

choices.label: Ask for a football pitch instead
choices.desc: Spend the money on the kids.
choices.text: Instead of a parade, the town builds a new pitch with his name on the gate. Every Saturday, a hundred kids play on it.

scenarios.title: {SIB}'s Wedding
scenarios.text: {SIB} is getting married. The wedding is on a matchday. The family assumes he'll be there and has already printed the seating plan.
scenarios.prompt: Your {SIBr}'s wedding clashes with a match.

choices.label: Ask the club for permission to miss the match
choices.hint: Most managers say yes to weddings.
choices.text: {M} grumbles and says yes. He's at the wedding, dances with {MUM}, and pays for the band.

choices.label: Play, and arrive for the reception
choices.text: He plays, showers in four minutes and arrives in time for the speeches, still sweaty. {SIB} doesn't care. {SIBhe}'s just glad he came.

choices.label: Send a huge gift instead
choices.text: The gift is extravagant. The empty chair at the top table is more noticeable.

scenarios.title: {DAD}'s Heart
scenarios.text: {DAD} collapses at the market. A heart attack, small, the doctors say, as if any heart attack is small. He's stable. He's asking for his phone so he can watch {J}'s highlights.
scenarios.prompt: Your father has had a heart attack.

choices.label: Go home immediately
choices.text: He's at the hospital by evening. {DAD} pretends to be annoyed that he came. He holds his son's hand all night.

choices.label: Pay for the best cardiologist in the country
choices.desc: The best care money can buy.
choices.text: The best cardiologist in the country flies in. {DAD} is grumbling about the hospital food within a week. A good sign.

scenarios.title: {DAD}
scenarios.text: The call comes at 5am. {DAD} died in his sleep. {MUM}'s voice is very calm, the way people sound when they haven't understood yet.
scenarios.prompt: Your father has died.

choices.label: Go home for as long as it takes
choices.text: He goes home for two weeks. He carries the coffin. He sleeps in his childhood bed and wakes up forgetting, every morning, for a second.

choices.label: Play the next match for him
choices.desc: It's what he would have wanted.
choices.text: He plays with a black armband. When he scores, he points at the sky and falls to his knees. Forty thousand people go silent, then applaud.

scenarios.title: The Land
scenarios.text: After the funeral, an uncle produces a document about the family land. Suddenly cousins he has never met have opinions about who owns what. {MUM} just wants it to stop.
scenarios.prompt: A family fight over the inheritance.

choices.label: Give up your share to {MUM}
choices.text: He signs his share over to {MUM} and tells the uncle the matter is closed. It isn't closed for the uncle, but it is for {J}.

choices.label: Hire a lawyer to settle it properly
choices.text: A lawyer sorts it out in three months. Everyone gets what's fair. Some relatives never speak to each other again.

scenarios.title: {MUM}'s Friend
scenarios.text: {MUM} has been 'going for walks' with a widower from the mosque. {SIB} is outraged. {MUM} is happier than she's been in years. Everyone is waiting to see what {J} says.
scenarios.prompt: Your mother has found someone new.

choices.label: Give her your blessing
choices.text: He invites the man for dinner. He's kind and nervous and supports the wrong club. {MUM} glows all evening.

choices.label: Ask for time
choices.text: {MUM} says she understands. She keeps going on walks. Quietly.

scenarios.title: {MUM} in a Foreign Country
scenarios.text: {MUM} has been living with him abroad for a while now. She can't read the signs, the supermarket doesn't sell anything she cooks with, and she's lonely while he's at training.
scenarios.prompt: Your mother is struggling abroad.

choices.label: Find her a community from home
choices.desc: Other families, a mosque or church, a market.
choices.text: He finds a small community from home. {MUM} has three new best friends within a month and a cooking group on Thursdays.

choices.label: Hire a driver and a translator for her
choices.text: With a driver and a translator, {MUM} explores the city. She knows more of it than he does by spring.

choices.label: Suggest she goes home for a while
choices.text: She goes home for the summer and comes back in autumn with three suitcases of spices. It works.

scenarios.title: Using Your Name
scenarios.text: A cousin has been selling 'signed' shirts and 'meet {J}' packages online, using family photos. Some buyers have paid a lot of money. None of them will ever meet him.
scenarios.prompt: A relative is scamming people using your name.

choices.label: Make it right with the buyers
choices.text: He refunds every buyer and meets the ones who paid most. The cousin is no longer invited to anything.

choices.label: Report it to the police
choices.text: The cousin is charged. Half the family takes the cousin's side. {MUM} takes {J}'s.

choices.label: Handle it inside the family
choices.text: The cousin cries and promises to stop. The online shop reopens under a different name a month later.

scenarios.title: Forty-Two Tickets
scenarios.text: The family group chat has decided they're all coming to Saturday's match. All forty-two of them. Each player gets four tickets.
scenarios.prompt: Your family wants forty-two tickets.

choices.label: Buy thirty-eight tickets
choices.text: Forty-two relatives in matching homemade shirts. They are the loudest section of the stadium. {J} can hear his aunt from the penalty spot.

choices.label: Four tickets, and {MUM} chooses
choices.text: {MUM} chooses the four. The rest of the family holds a viewing party at an uncle's house and complains loudly.

scenarios.title: {SIB}'s New Partner
scenarios.text: {SIB} has a new partner and is serious about them. {J} met them once and didn't like them: too interested in his car, his contacts, his money.
scenarios.prompt: You don't trust your {SIBr}'s new partner.

out.text: {SIB} is furious. Then, a month later, {SIBhe} admits {SIBhe} had doubts too. They break up.
{SIB} chooses the partner. They don't speak for a year.

choices.label: Give them a chance
choices.text: He makes an effort. The partner is nervous around famous people, it turns out, not greedy. They become friends.

scenarios.title: Coach
scenarios.text: His first coach, the man who gave him boots when his family couldn't afford them, is dying. He's in a small hospital in his hometown. He doesn't want a fuss.
scenarios.prompt: Your first coach is dying.

choices.label: Visit him
choices.desc: Bring the boots he gave you.
choices.hint: Say thank you while you can.
choices.text: He brings the old boots, now framed. The coach laughs, then cries, then makes him promise to keep running. He dies a week later.

choices.label: Pay for his care, anonymously
choices.text: The bills are paid. The coach never knows who paid. His widow figures it out and sends a letter.

scenarios.title: Their House
scenarios.text: {MUM} and {DAD} have been in the new house for a while now. {DAD} has planted mango trees. {MUM} has hung every photo of {J} ever taken in the hallway, including some he'd hoped had been destroyed.
scenarios.prompt: Visit your parents in their new home.

choices.label: Stay for the weekend
choices.text: {DAD} gives him a tour of every tree. {MUM} cooks for twelve. He sleeps ten hours. It is the most restful weekend of the year.

choices.label: Help with the garden
choices.text: They dig all afternoon and barely speak. It's the best conversation they've had in years.

scenarios.title: {KID} at School
scenarios.text: {KID}'s teacher calls: other children are teasing {KID} about {J}'s last bad match. {KID} got into a fight defending {J}'s honour.
scenarios.prompt: Your child is being teased because of you.

choices.label: Visit the school and talk to the class
choices.text: He visits the class, signs everyone's books, and talks about losing and getting back up. {KID} has never been more popular.

choices.label: Talk to {KID} about fame
choices.text: He tells {KID} that people will always talk, and that what matters is what we know about ourselves. {KID} listens. Mostly.

scenarios.title: {KID} Wants to Be Like You
scenarios.text: {KID} has started wearing {J}'s shirt to bed and practising celebrations in the garden. Today {KID} asked, 'Can I be a footballer too?'
scenarios.prompt: Your child wants to follow in your footsteps.

choices.label: Say yes, and make it fun
choices.text: Saturday mornings in the park become sacred. {KID} isn't especially good. {KID} is very happy.

choices.label: Encourage other things too
choices.text: Football, piano and painting. {KID} chooses painting. {J} has a painting of himself scoring on his fridge.

scenarios.title: {MUM}'s Birthday
scenarios.text: {MUM} turns {MUMage} this week. She says she doesn't want anything. She has said this every year and meant it zero times.
scenarios.prompt: How do you mark {MUM}'s birthday?

choices.label: Surprise her in person
choices.text: He turns up with flowers and her favourite cake. She screams, then cries, then tells him he should have warned her because the house is a mess.

choices.label: Send something she'd never buy herself
choices.text: A beautiful gift arrives with a handwritten note. She calls to say it's too much and wears it to church on Sunday.

choices.label: Forget until the evening
choices.hint: {MUM} will say it's fine. It's not fine.
choices.text: He remembers at 9pm. She says it's fine. {SIB} says it is absolutely not fine.

scenarios.title: {DAD}'s Old Dream
scenarios.text: Over dinner, {DAD} mentions, almost by accident, that he always wanted to see a World Cup match in person. He laughs it off. {J} doesn't.
scenarios.prompt: Make your father's dream come true?

choices.label: Take him to the next big tournament
choices.text: {DAD} sings every anthem, cries at a match between two countries he has no connection to, and talks about it for the rest of his life.

choices.label: Take him to a big match in your league
choices.desc: The best seats in the house.
choices.text: Best seats, a stadium tour, a handshake with a legend. {DAD} keeps the ticket in his wallet forever.

scenarios.title: The Family Group Chat
text: The extended family group chat has 147 members and has turned into a war over his last match. One uncle thinks he should be dropped. An aunt has posted a prayer. {MUM} has left the chat twice.
Someone in the family group chat has forwarded a fake news story about him. Three aunts believe it.
scenarios.prompt: The family group chat is chaos.

choices.label: Post a calm message to everyone
choices.text: His message is polite and clear. It's followed by forty-six stickers of praying hands and one uncle asking for tickets.

choices.label: Mute it forever
choices.text: Muted. Bliss. {MUM} reports the highlights at dinner.

scenarios.title: Mudik
text: Lebaran is coming. The whole country is going home, and the roads out of the city are already a parking lot. {MUM} has asked, three times, whether he's coming.
Lebaran: the one time of year everyone goes home. The club has a match two days after Idul Fitri. The journey home takes fourteen hours in this traffic.
scenarios.prompt: Go home for Lebaran?

choices.label: Go home, whatever the traffic
choices.text: Fourteen hours in a car, then the whole family, ketupat and forgiveness. He kneels before {MUM} and {DAD} and asks for forgiveness for the year. Everyone cries.

choices.label: Fly the family to you instead
choices.text: He flies everyone in. Lebaran in a rented villa. {MUM} says it isn't the same, then has the best time of her life.

choices.label: Stay and focus on the match
choices.text: He video-calls the whole family on Idul Fitri. {MUM} holds the phone up to every relative one by one. It takes two hours.

scenarios.title: {MUM}'s Arisan
scenarios.text: {MUM}'s monthly arisan group, twenty women who have known each other for thirty years, has asked whether her famous son might drop by. It is not really a question.
scenarios.prompt: Visit your mother's arisan?

choices.label: Go, and charm every auntie
choices.text: Two hours, forty selfies, nine offers to introduce him to someone's niece. {MUM}'s status in the group is now permanently the highest.

choices.label: Send signed photos for everyone
choices.text: Twenty signed photos, each personalised. The aunties accept the compromise, mostly.

scenarios.title: The Whole Village
scenarios.text: The village where his parents grew up has heard he's rich. A delegation of elders arrives at his parents' house with a list: a new mosque roof, a road, a well, school uniforms.
scenarios.prompt: The village wants your help.

choices.label: Fund the school and the well
choices.text: The well is dug and the uniforms arrive. A plaque with his name goes up by the school gate. {DAD} visits it every month.

choices.label: Fund everything on the list
choices.text: Everything on the list, done. The village names a street after him. A second list arrives the following year.

choices.label: Explain you can't do it all
choices.text: He explains kindly. Some elders understand. Some tell the village he's forgotten where he came from.

scenarios.title: {SIB} the Influencer
scenarios.text: {SIB} has started an account called '{J}'s {SIBr}'. It has three hundred thousand followers. {SIBhe} is posting family photos and stories {J} would rather keep private.
scenarios.prompt: Your {SIBr} is getting famous off your name.

choices.label: Set some ground rules together
choices.text: They agree on rules: no photos of {MUM} without asking, no stories about his relationships. {SIB}'s account keeps growing anyway.

choices.label: Ask {SIBhim} to stop
choices.text: 'It's my career,' {SIB} says. 'You don't get to own our family.' Ouch. Fair.

choices.label: Collaborate with {SIBhim}
choices.text: Their joint video, {SIB} roasting {J}'s cooking, gets five million views. Their mother is in the background, shaking her head.

scenarios.title: Thirty Years
scenarios.text: {MUM} and {DAD} have been married for thirty years this month. They've never had a honeymoon. They had a wedding in a rented hall and went back to work the next day.
scenarios.prompt: Their thirtieth anniversary.

choices.label: Send them on the honeymoon they never had
choices.text: Ten days somewhere with a sea. {DAD} sends one photo a day, every one of them of {MUM}.

choices.label: Throw them a big party
choices.text: Two hundred guests, a band, the first dance they never had. {DAD} cries during his speech.

scenarios.title: A Box From Home
scenarios.text: A box arrives from {MUM}: sambal, dried fish, spices, a letter, and his favourite snacks wrapped in newspaper. Customs has opened it. Customs has kept the sambal.
scenarios.prompt: A care package from home.

choices.label: Call her and cry a little
choices.text: He calls her holding the letter. They both cry a bit. Then she asks whether he's eating vegetables.

choices.label: Share it with the squad
choices.desc: A taste of home for everyone.
choices.text: He shares the snacks with the squad. The Dutch goalkeeper is now addicted to them. {MUM} is told and is thrilled.

scenarios.title: The Interview
scenarios.text: {DAD}, hurt that {J} hasn't called in months, gives a local TV station an interview: 'My son has changed. Money changed him.' The clip is everywhere.
scenarios.prompt: Your father criticised you on TV.

choices.label: Go home and talk to him
choices.text: He goes home. {DAD} opens the door, and for a moment neither of them speaks. Then {DAD} hugs him. They talk all night.

choices.label: Respond publicly
choices.text: His response is measured. It doesn't matter. The feud becomes a soap opera in the tabloids.

choices.label: Say nothing at all
choices.text: He says nothing. {DAD} watches his son's next match on TV and calls him the next day, quietly.
